_meta.dataset: PolicyCentral RBI Enforcement Tracker, FY26-27 records
_meta.source: RBI press releases on rbi.org.in (BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx), 1 April to 18 September 2026, read directly from the source pages
_meta.coverage: Scheduled commercial banks (including one regional rural bank), payments banks, NBFCs, HFCs, ARCs, payment system operators, PPI issuers and credit information companies. Co-operative banks and district central co-operative banks are out of scope. Bulk NBFC certificate-of-registration cancellations are not itemised.
_meta.note: cited_reasons are plain-language restatements of the charges RBI stated as sustained in the press release (facts only, no commentary). action_date is the date of the RBI order. penalty_amount_display uses the rupee sign. rbi_directions_cited lists the direction names as RBI quoted them.

cited_reasons.text: Breached the permissible leverage ratio limit.
Did not submit certain supervisory returns to RBI at the prescribed frequency and within the stipulated timelines.
Did not furnish its balance sheet to RBI within the stipulated period.

records.scope_note: Return-filing calendars and deadline ownership are a policy and process matter; the leverage breach is not.

cited_reasons.text: Did not carry out risk categorisation of its customers.

records.scope_note: Risk categorisation is a KYC policy obligation that staff must know and apply.

cited_reasons.text: Did not disclose in application forms and sanction letters the approach for gradation of risk and the rationale for charging different interest rates to different categories of borrowers.

records.scope_note: A disclosure that lives in the loan application form and sanction letter template; a policy-distribution failure.

cited_reasons.text: Did not carry out periodic review of the risk categorisation of certain categories of accounts.
Sanctioned director-related loans, in contravention of section 20(1)(b)(iii) of the Banking Regulation Act.

records.scope_note: The KYC review cycle is policy-driven; director-related lending is a credit-governance control.

cited_reasons.text: RBI cancelled its banking licence under section 22(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, effective from close of business on 24 April 2026, finding that its affairs were conducted in a manner detrimental to the interest of the bank and its depositors, that the general character of its management was prejudicial to the interest of depositors and the public, that no useful purpose would be served by allowing it to continue, and that it had failed to comply with the conditions of its payments bank licence. RBI stated that the bank has enough liquidity to repay its entire deposit liability and that it will apply to the High Court for winding up.

records.scope_note: A supervisory finding on the conduct of the bank as a whole, not a single policy control.
